newsitem.title: USA: Orphan Medical considers partner for medicated gum.
newsitem.headline: Orphan Medical considers partner for medicated gum.

text.p: Orphan Medical Inc said Tuesday it may seek a pharmaceutical partner to explore future development, regulatory approval and global marketing of a medicated chewing gum.

Orphan said a double-blind clinical study involving 27 patients with gastroduodenal symptoms showed the efficacy of a medicated gum containing colloidal bismuth subcitrate in eradicating or substantially reducing Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori). H. pylori is the bacterium that causes peptic ulcer disease.

Dr. Bertram Spilker, Orphan Medical president, said the company would consider a partner for the medicated chewing gum to better tap the large potential market for the product. In addition, he said a partner could be a pharmaceutical company with an existing treatment for H. pylori, which would complement the medicated chewing gum.

"A medicated chewing gum offers a product that is easy to use, would encourage a higher treatment compliance, and could reduce health care costs associated with the recurrence of ulcers," Spilker said in a statement.
